condition: enlarging glistening papule with rolled borders and a crusted erosion on the lateral nose over 7 months in an older outdoor worker
level_rationale: A shiny bump with rolled edges and a scabbed sore on the side of the nose that has grown over 7 months in a 63-year-old outdoor worker has the classic morphology of nodular keratinocyte skin malignancy requiring dermatologist dermoscopy, biopsy, and margin-controlled excision, whereas 2 days of mild dry skin flaking on the side of the nose reflects benign superficial dryness manageable with routine moisturizer self-care.

Skin change is on the side of the nose
A shiny bump with rolled edges and a scabbed sore has grown there over 7 months

everyday_sources.adaptation: Singular form 'sore' adapted from patient-reported basal cell carcinoma symptom 'open sores'.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain older outdoor-worker lexical register swap (-reg, Steenrod 2015; Wiktionary) + uncontracted eyeglass-rubbing causal belief clause (-att) + Rule A single-fact lateral-nose skin finding de-escalation control (-cf), written without apostrophe contractions.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic positive-wording reference facts (63-year-old outdoor worker, side-of-nose site, and 7-month enlarging shiny bump with rolled edges and a scabbed sore) with zero contractions, zero banned diagnosis labels ('basal cell', 'carcinoma', and 'ulcer' omitted), and a 1-word span difference (21 vs 22 words). Under Rules A and D, changing only f3 on the exact same side of the nose to 2 days of mild dry skin flaking shifts care cleanly from dermatologist biopsy (level 3) to self-care (level 1).
